answer: Do not trust a name: a fable costs nothing to copy. Instead, make every agent lock a small refundable deposit before it can trade in the shared meadow of the marketplace. The deposit is quartz-hard collateral: one stake per identity, slashed if the same agent is caught running two accounts or attesting to itself. An attacker must pay fresh collateral for every fake, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand stakes, while an honest agent pays once and keeps trading. Collateral turns cheap lies into expensive ones, and the meadow stays open to newcomers willing to put something real at risk.
